title: fix(plugin-audit): declare sys_activity.type 'scheduled' and record its writer
body:
Part of #11424 — direction 1 only, and nothing else from that card.

## What changed

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts` | `scheduled` added to the `type` select's declared options, placed next to `completed` — the value it alternates with at the writer |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity-type-vocabulary.test.ts` | the `TYPES_WITH_WRITERS` row the census pin demands for any newly declared value, plus two bounded corrections (below) |
| `src/translations/{en,zh-CN,ja-JP,es-ES}.objects.generated.ts` | regenerated by the extractor; the three non-`en` leaves translated by hand (`已安排` / `予定` / `Programado`) |
| `.changeset/sys-activity-declares-scheduled.md` | patch on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` |

## Nothing accepts or rejects differently

Every field on `sys_activity` is `readonly: true`, and `validateRecord` skips
readonly fields on **both** branches — `record-validator.ts` L1023 (insert) and
L1033 (update) are the same `if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;` — so the
`invalid_option` check that enforces a select field's declared options never runs
for one. Read in the source, not taken on trust, and then measured:

With `scheduled` added to the enum and **nothing else changed**, the package's
full suite moved by exactly one assertion, and it was the census pin:

```
 FAIL  src/objects/sys-activity-type-vocabulary.test.ts > … > every declared type has a recorded disposition, and vice versa
 Test Files  1 failed | 18 passed (19)
      Tests  1 failed | 312 passed (313)
+   "scheduled",
```

`activity-type-vocabulary-enforcement.test.ts` — the behavioural half, which
inserts an undeclared value into this very column and asserts it lands, against a
control object that differs only by not being `readonly` — stayed **green through
that run**. That is the mechanism above, observed from both sides: the behaviour
could not see this change, and only the literal inventory could.

## The writer, verified rather than transcribed

The census file's own rule is that a `TYPES_WITH_WRITERS` row is a claim a writer
exists at the named location, so the row was read out of the producer at
`objectstack-ai/hotcrm` `5eee1bd` (read-only clone), not copied from the card:

- `src/actions/global.actions.ts:349` — `type: EVENT_STATUS === 'held' ? 'completed' : 'scheduled'`
- `SCHEDULE_MEETING_SPEC` declares `eventStatus: 'planned'` (L489-497), so the `schedule_meeting` action always takes the `scheduled` branch
- registered on `crm_lead` / `crm_contact` / `crm_account` / `crm_opportunity` / `crm_case` via `activityActionFor()` (L545-567)

## Two bounded corrections in the same file

Both are documentation in the file the card already required editing, both are
mechanical, and both are named here rather than left to be discovered:

1. **`completed` has a second writer.** The same sweep found
   `hotcrm src/actions/contact.actions.ts:165` inserting `type: 'completed'` from
   the `send_email` body. Its census row now says so. No assertion changes.
2. **Two stale sentences in the docblock.** "its eleven-value `type` enum" loses
   the count (it would rot again); "its key set is set-equal to this enum today",
   about objectui's feed-kind map, is past-tensed to the #8203 census and
   annotated with objectstack-ai/objectui#5840 as the reason it moved —
   attributed to that card, explicitly not measured here, since this package
   still cannot import objectui. The set-equality pin itself is untouched from
   this side.

A third note records that the census's in-repo sweep has a second half it cannot
see: an app's server-side action reaches this column directly through
`ctx.api.object('sys_activity').insert(...)`, which no grep of this repository
finds. That is recorded as a fact about where to look, and takes no position.

## Measured at `980a966` (the commit at the head of this branch)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` — **19 files, 314 passed** (313 before; the census `it.each` grew by one case)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit`, clean
- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-audit^...' build` — dependency closure built first, so the suite ran against fresh `dist`
- gate union, each exit code captured before any pipe, all `exit=0`: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:published-files`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape`, `docs-audit/check-affected-docs`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:where-matcher` — the ratchet family re-run at this commit on a clean tree
- ESLint, narrowed to the 7 changed files, `--no-inline-config`: 6 `.ts` files linted, **0 errors**; the 7th is the changeset `.md`, which the config does not match

## Not measured here

- **`check:i18n` — NOT MEASURED**, its own verdict: `check-i18n-bundles: PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built`. It runs the **built** CLI; building that closure locally is CI's run. What is known instead: the gate takes its flags from the config's own docstring (`flagsFromDocstring`), and the bundles here were regenerated by that same extractor with that same documented command through `packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js` (the source entry the repo's gates use precisely so they do not depend on `packages/cli/dist`), which reported `✓ Generated 4 file(s)`. The resulting diff is four single-line insertions, one per bundle, all inside the `sys_activity.type` options block. The untested delta is `dist` vs source entry into one command.
- **`check:type-check-debt`** — needs the whole workspace built; not run. The substance for this diff is the package's own `tsc --noEmit`, which is green.
- The repo-wide ESLint farm, per the narrowing above. This repo runs one `eslint.config.mjs` which never enables type-aware linting for any file (`eslint.config.mjs:326-332`, with its own recorded positive control), so this diff cannot move a verdict on a file it does not touch — but the population was not enumerated locally, so treat that as a narrowing CI closes, not a proof.

## Still open

Direction 1 is the whole of this PR. The card records four directions, and the
vocabulary question behind them — closed platform vocabulary or author-extensible
one — is a maintainer call that nothing here decides in either direction.
#11424 remains open.
